extracted.intended_audience: screenwriters and other writers seeking to document and protect authorship of creative works
extracted.subtask_description: Information and procedural standards for registering scripts and other creative files with the Writers Guild of America West Registry to document authorship and create dated legal evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is registration / purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Registering your work with the WGAW Registry documents the claim of authorship of a written work and does NOT take the place of registering with the Library of Congress, U.S. Copyright Office which primarily documents the ownership or rights of written work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both WGAW registration and Library of Congress registration create legal evidence that can be used in court; contact the Library of Congress directly with any questions regarding COPYRIGHT procedures or practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of registration as dated evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration provides a dated record of the writer's claim to authorship of literary material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you register your script prior to submitting it to contests, agents, managers, or producers, you document your authorship on a given date should there be unauthorized usage. The WGAW Registry may produce the material as evidence if legal action is initiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: What can be registered / acceptable materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Any file may be registered to assist you in documenting the creation of your work. Some examples of registerable material include scripts, treatments, synopses, and outlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The WGAW Registry also accepts stageplays, novels, books, short stories, poems, commercials, lyrics, drawings, music and various media work such as Web series, code, and other digital content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to Library of Congress registration
rubrics_metrics.description: WGAW registration does NOT take the place of registering with the Library of Congress, U.S. Copyright Office, which primarily documents ownership or rights of written work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While both create legal evidence, the WGAW Registry recommends contacting the Library of Congress for questions about copyright procedures; consider both registrations depending on your legal needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility / membership requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You do not need to be a WGAW member to use this vital Guild service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the WGA West is the home to nearly 12,000 of Hollywood's leading TV and screenwriters, the Registry service is available to non-members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format and operational limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The WGAW Registry is not open to the public. Paper material is not accepted. In-person services are not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must be electronic (no paper); the Registry is accessed remotely rather than via public or in-person walk-in services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and support information
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact details are provided for Registry assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WGAW Registry phone: (323) 782-4500; email: WGAW Registry — use these channels for questions about registration, renewals, and the service.
